question: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q3 FY2027 earnings release? (Gross margin (GAAP))

calls.reasoning: On the Aug 26, 2026 Q2 FY27 call, Nvidia explicitly said gross margin would fall to 74% in Q3 and bottom at 71-72% in Q4 FY27, driven by memory costs. Nvidia's past pre-signals (low-70s in early FY26, mid-70s by end of FY26) translated nearly exactly into subsequent guides. GAAP and non-GAAP are now guided identically, so GAAP ≈ non-GAAP. Median at the 71.5 midpoint; downside risk if memory costs worsened further, upside if pricing/mix offsets. Polymarket markets found concern Q3 actual non-GAAP GM (73-75% at 0.87), a near-miss contract consistent with the Q3 guide but not an anchor for the Q4 GAAP guide; no market on the Q4 guide found.
sources: polymarket.com NVDA Q3 adjusted gross margin markets (harness-listed)
calls.dossier:
- Q2 FY27 press release (Aug 26, 2026, nvidianews): Q2 GAAP and non-GAAP GM both 75.0%; Q3 FY27 outlook GAAP and non-GAAP GM both 74.0% +/-50bp; revenue $108.0B +/-2%; no China DC compute assumed.
- Q2 FY27 call (Aug 26, 2026; TheElec, GamesReviews, Yahoo UK preview): management said GM 'expected to be 74% in the third quarter ... and fall to 71% to 72% in the fourth quarter'; memory price increases exceeded prior expectations and are headed higher next year; recovery expected in FY28 as higher prices take effect.
- Kress quote: 'We want to be direct about this, rather than let it linger as an open question.'
- Historical pre-signal behavior: early FY26 said GM 'low 70s' during Blackwell ramp -> Q1 FY26 guide 71.0% non-GAAP / 70.6% GAAP; later said 'mid-70s' by year end -> Q4 FY26 guide 75.0% non-GAAP / 74.8% GAAP (Q4 FY26 actual GAAP 75.0%, non-GAAP 75.2%).
- GAAP vs non-GAAP gap: historically 0.1-0.4pt (GAAP lower); in Q2/Q3 FY27 guidance they are identical.
- Q3 FY27 report scheduled Nov 17, 2026 after close; consensus revenue ~$109B (Yahoo UK preview).
- Status quo: guide consistent with the 71-72% pre-signal (midpoint 71.5).
- Resolution: midpoint of GAAP GM range in the 'Outlook' section of the Q3 FY27 press release, rounded to 0.1%; not non-GAAP, not CFO commentary.
- Event window: single event on Nov 17, 2026 release; as of Nov 6, 2026 the release has not occurred.
- Searched but not found: any intra-quarter (Sept-Oct 2026) update from management revising the 71-72% Q4 commentary; sell-side consensus for Q4 GM guide specifically; any human market on the Q4 GM guide.
calls.reference_class: Nvidia quarterly GM guidance following explicit management pre-signals of the next-next quarter margin level (FY25-FY27)

calls.reasoning: On the Aug 26, 2026 Q2 FY27 call, NVIDIA guided Q3 GM to 74.0% ±50bp and said margins would bottom at 71-72% in Q4 because memory costs rose more than expected. NVIDIA usually guides to round numbers, so a 71.5% ±50bp guide fits the stated range best; 72.0% and 71.0% are the next most likely. Further memory inflation (the CFO said prices keep rising into next year) is a downside risk; pricing or mix upside could give 72.0-72.5. GAAP has sometimes sat ~0.2pt below non-GAAP, though they are equal lately. Markets: only Polymarket contracts on Q3 actual non-GAAP GM (73-75% at 0.87) were found, not Q4 guidance, so I used them as evidence rather than an anchor; no matching market found.

The formal guide usually lands near the preview midpoint, so the anchor is 71.5%. Downside: memory costs keep rising and GAAP can run 0.1-0.3pt below non-GAAP. calls.reasoning: On the Aug 26, 2026 call NVIDIA said GM would bottom at 71-72% in Q4 FY27 because of memory costs. Its past previews became formal guides almost exactly, and it guides a point ±50bp at X.0/X.5, so 71.5% is the main case, with 71.0 and 72.0 next. GAAP has matched non-GAAP in the last two guides but historically ran 0.1-0.4pt lower, giving a slight downside lean. Rising memory costs are the downside risk; pricing and mix could lift the guide to 72.0. Market check: only Polymarket contracts on Q3 actual non-GAAP GM exist (73-75% at 0.87, low volume), which supports the Q3 guide but is not an anchor here; no market on the Q4 GAAP guide was found.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the facts: Q3 guide 74.0% ±50bp with GAAP = non-GAAP, a 71-72% Q4 preview on the Aug 26 call, and no update to it found since. Disputes were judgment only: tail width (1.1-1.5) and how much weight to give GAAP sitting below non-GAAP. Whether 71-72% refers to GAAP or non-GAAP cannot be settled from the dossiers, so it carries modest downside weight. I kept the 71.5 median and run 3's reference class, with a slightly downside-skewed width of 1.3. No web access on this run, so nothing new was retrieved.

disagreements.claim: Width of the 10-90 interval (1.1 vs 1.4 vs 1.5)
disagreements.verdict: Set at 1.3: the guide is a discrete X.0/X.5 point next to a firm preview, so tails stay narrow but 71.0/72.0 remain live

disagreements.verdict: Not settled by the dossiers; immaterial if equal, as in recent guides

disagreements.verdict: About 1% each side, since a far-off revision is unlikely given the explicit preview
